name: Lakota'mani
summary: At Camp Taurajo, hunters bring Lakota'mani's hoof to Jorn Skyseer after the hunt. The offering honors the mighty kodo's spirit and marks the hunter as an equal to its strength.

sections.title: The Earthshaker
sections.body: Among the Barrens herds, Lakota'mani is a kodo of great size and endurance. In Taur-ahe, the tauren tongue, his name means “Earthshaker,” and his steps rumble across the plains. Tauren hunters track and defeat such a beast not for slaughter, but to meet the raw vigor of Kalimdor's wildlife in a sacred hunt.

sections.title: A Hunt Honored at Camp Taurajo
sections.body: When you bring Lakota'mani's hoof to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, the hunt reaches its close. Jorn sees a new power and stride in hunters who return from the encounter. Presenting the trophy earns his blessing, honoring Lakota'mani's courage and primal spirit as companions on your path.

faq.q: What does the name Lakota'mani mean?
aliases: what does lakotamani mean in taurahe
faq.answer: Lakota'mani means “Earthshaker” in Taur-ahe, the tauren tongue. The name fits the beast's immense size and the thunderous rumble of his steps across the plains.
Jorn Skyseer is a tauren elder and spiritual guide at Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens. He reads signs, guides young hunters, and honors the great beasts slain across the plains.

faq.q: Why do tauren collect the hooves of great beasts?
faq.answer: Tauren hunters carry a great beast's hoof as a token of its power. Presenting it to an elder honors the fallen beast's spirit and fortitude alongside the hunter's own.

faq.q: Where does the beast Lakota'mani roam?
faq.answer: Lakota'mani roams the open savanna of the central and southern Barrens, among the lesser kodo herds, until an attentive hunter tracks him down.

faq.q: Why does Jorn call the hunter 'Earthshaker'?
faq.answer: Jorn Skyseer calls the hunter “Earthshaker” because besting Lakota'mani joins the beast's spirit and courage with the hunter's own. The hunter takes on the name and walks with the same thunderous resolve.

faq.q: Does this hunt have spiritual significance beyond Camp Taurajo?
faq.answer: Yes. The hunt reflects the tauren belief in the Earthmother and the natural balance. By testing themselves against nature's greatest avatars, hunters prove their strength and carry that spiritual strength into future conflicts.

angles.text: As a tauren hunter, defeating Lakota'mani fulfills an ancient hunting tradition and earns reverence and the proud title of Earthshaker from your elders.
As a hunter, tracking a legendary solitary kodo across the vast savanna tests your tracking skill, endurance, and field combat in the heart of Kalimdor.
Camp Taurajo is a hunting hub for the Horde. Claiming the plains' spoils helps build your reputation among the tribes.
